name: The Great Lakes
tagline: The big water keeps what it takes

entry.title: THE FANG MARK · CASE 001
entry.body: Field note: item recovered off the trail past Bray Road. Condition inconsistent with time exposed. Recommend cross-reference with prior cases.

entry.title: THE FOG-DAMP FISH HOOK · CASE 002
entry.body: Field note: item recovered off the trail past the Ore Docks. Condition inconsistent with time exposed. Recommend cross-reference with prior cases.

entry.title: THE MAGNIFYING GLASS · CASE 003
entry.body: We found the Magnifying Glass on the second day. Whatever left it there had come back through Sleeping Bear that same night. The prints went right past our tent.

entry.title: THE PROPELLER · CASE 004
entry.body: My uncle kept it in a drawer since 1955. Would not say where he got it. After he passed, I found the map it was wrapped in.

puzzles.name: Minnow Bucket of the Manistee Woods
puzzles.subtitle: Bray Road

entry.title: MINNOW BUCKET OF THE MANISTEE WOODS · CASE 005
entry.body: Recovered near the Ferry Line, 1970. Bagged, tagged, photographed. Nothing about where it lay makes sense. The file stays open.

entry.title: THE WAVE-WORN LOST MITTEN · CASE 006
entry.body: It was just sitting there, out past Isle Royale, like it had been left for someone to find. Maybe it was. Maybe that someone was me.

entry.title: THE SUSPENSION BRIDGE · CASE 007
entry.body: Of the Suspension Bridge near the Ore Docks the older maps say nothing, though it has stood, by every local account, since before the maps were drawn.

entry.title: THE DIVING HELMET · CASE 008
entry.body: Catalogued 1941. The Diving Helmet was exactly where the witness said it would be. That is the part that bothers me.

entry.title: THE WAVE-WORN FILM STRIP · CASE 009
entry.body: Field note: item recovered off the trail past Copper Harbor. Condition inconsistent with time exposed. Recommend cross-reference with prior cases.

entry.title: ICE SKATE OF COPPER HARBOR · CASE 010
entry.body: Catalogued 1996. The Ice Skate of Copper Harbor was exactly where the witness said it would be. That is the part that bothers me.

entry.title: THE PAW PRINT · CASE 011
entry.body: Our party came upon the Paw Print near the Ferry Line, abandoned in circumstances I hesitate to record. We carried it out; none among us would carry it twice.

entry.title: THE SHIP'S BELL · CASE 012
entry.body: Item logged 1975. Chain of custody: incomplete. Explanation on file: none. Status: unresolved, like the rest of the drawer.

entry.title: THE ANCHOR · CASE 013
entry.body: My uncle kept it in a drawer since 1968. Would not say where he got it. After he passed, I found the map it was wrapped in.

entry.title: THE FISHING LURE · CASE 014
entry.body: Let this entry attest that the article was found at Superior Shoals, untouched by weather in a season of storms. Philosophy offers no account of it.

entry.title: LIFE RING OF WHITEFISH POINT · CASE 015
entry.body: One Life Ring of Whitefish Point, recovered at Copper Harbor. No owner came forward. Per policy, unclaimed evidence is destroyed after ninety days. This item has been in storage since 1963.

entry.title: THE RUST-PITTED OAR · CASE 016
entry.body: Recovered near the North Channel, 1975. Bagged, tagged, photographed. Nothing about where it lay makes sense. The file stays open.

entry.title: THE SNOWSHOE · CASE 017
entry.body: Item logged 1980. Chain of custody: incomplete. Explanation on file: none. Status: unresolved, like the rest of the drawer.

entry.title: CANOE OF SLEEPING BEAR · CASE 018
entry.body: Found at the Manistee Woods. Standard recovery, non-standard circumstances. The report uses the word "placed" where "dropped" was expected.

puzzles.name: Black Bear Cub of the Ferry Line
puzzles.subtitle: Superior Shoals

entry.title: BLACK BEAR CUB OF THE FERRY LINE · CASE 019
entry.body: A dark shape off Isle Royale. Three witnesses, one photograph, no clear resolution. The report was filed and, per policy, quietly closed.

entry.title: ICE AUGER OF SUPERIOR SHOALS · CASE 020
entry.body: Let this entry attest that the article was found at Sleeping Bear, untouched by weather in a season of storms. Philosophy offers no account of it.

entry.title: THE AMBER-EYED SNOWSHOE HARE · CASE 021
entry.body: A dark shape off the North Channel. Three witnesses, one photograph, no clear resolution. The report was filed and, per policy, quietly closed.

entry.title: THE FRESHWATER MONARCH BUTTERFLY · CASE 022
entry.body: My grandfather saw it first. Now I have too, plain as day, out by Bray Road. Whatever the Freshwater Monarch Butterfly is, it remembers this valley.

entry.title: THE CHANNEL BUOY · CASE 023
entry.body: Let this entry attest that the article was found at Superior Shoals, untouched by weather in a season of storms. Philosophy offers no account of it.

entry.title: THE FOG-GREY PAINTED TURTLE · CASE 024
entry.body: Field note: heavy sign along the Ore Docks. Snapped branches at eight feet. Smell of wet copper. Did not linger to confirm.

entry.title: THE YELLOW PERCH · CASE 025
entry.body: Duration of sighting: under a minute. Location: the North Channel. Conclusion: inconclusive, which is the only honest word for it.

entry.title: BALD EAGLE OF WHITEFISH POINT · CASE 026
entry.body: Report from the Manistee Woods: a shape too large for any bear, moving without sound. No scat, no den. Witness sober. Logged as Bald Eagle of Whitefish Point.

entry.title: THE HERRING GULL · CASE 027
entry.body: The Herring Gull was logged as driftwood. Driftwood does not leave that kind of track. The file remains, uncorrected, in the drawer marked open.

entry.title: BEAVER OF COPPER HARBOR · CASE 028
entry.body: The guide would not speak its name above a whisper. Near Isle Royale we beheld the Beaver of Copper Harbor, and no man among us slept that night.

entry.title: THE FRESHWATER HERRING GULL · CASE 029

entry.title: THE AMBER-EYED GREAT BLUE HERON · CASE 031
entry.body: I set down this account of Bray Road that it may not be lost: a creature of the old accounts, thought a fable, stood not forty paces distant.

entry.title: THE RIVER OTTER · CASE 032

puzzles.name: The Freshwater Beast of Bray Road
puzzles.subtitle: Superior Shoals

entry.title: THE FRESHWATER BEAST OF BRAY ROAD · CASE 037
entry.body: A dark shape off the Ferry Line. Three witnesses, one photograph, no clear resolution. The report was filed and, per policy, quietly closed.

entry.title: THE STORM-DRIVEN GRAY WOLF · CASE 038
entry.body: Our party, encamped near Superior Shoals in the autumn of 2002, observed a figure of uncommon stature. It regarded us without fear, then withdrew as though it had never been.

entry.title: FISHING TRAWLER OF COPPER HARBOR · CASE 039
entry.body: We found the Fishing Trawler of Copper Harbor on the second day. Whatever left it there had come back through Whitefish Point that same night. The prints went right past our tent.

entry.title: THE ICE-FISHING HUT · CASE 040
entry.body: Structure logged near the Manistee Woods, 1967. Not on the registry. Not on the tax rolls. Not, per the county, anyone’s problem.

entry.title: LIGHTHOUSE OF SLEEPING BEAR · CASE 041
entry.body: Locals will not camp within sight of the Lighthouse of Sleeping Bear. When asked why, they answer a different question. Noted, 1941; still unexplained.

puzzles.name: Pictured Rocks Arch of Superior Shoals
puzzles.subtitle: Whitefish Point

entry.title: PICTURED ROCKS ARCH OF SUPERIOR SHOALS · CASE 042
entry.body: Let it be recorded that in 2004 the Pictured Rocks Arch of Superior Shoals was observed to stand dark and silent, though every account agrees it had no cause to be either.

entry.title: SHIPWRECK OF BRAY ROAD · CASE 043
entry.body: The Shipwreck of Bray Road was closer to the road than I remembered. The next morning it was farther. I stopped checking after that.

puzzles.name: Great Horned Owl of Isle Royale
puzzles.subtitle: the Ore Docks

entry.title: GREAT HORNED OWL OF ISLE ROYALE · CASE 044
entry.body: We were near Bray Road when the dogs quit barking all at once. That is when I saw it. I have not been back after dark since.

entry.title: THE SERPENTINE GREAT BLUE HERON · CASE 045

entry.title: THE BLACK BEAR · CASE 048
entry.body: Let the record show that on the road past Bray Road, in the year 1970, a thing was seen which philosophy cannot yet explain.

entry.title: THE GREY DOGMAN · CASE 051
entry.body: Observed 1987 near the Ferry Line. Approximately human height, not human gait. No further comment was offered by the witness or requested of them.

entry.title: THE ORE FREIGHTER · CASE 052
entry.body: Found at the Ore Docks: one The Ore Freighter, owner unknown. No tracks leading in. No tracks leading out. Logged and shelved.

entry.title: MOOSE OF THE ORE DOCKS · CASE 053
entry.body: I only saw it for a breath, out past Copper Harbor. It watched me the way a person watches, then stepped back into the dark and was just gone.
